en: 10. Indriyayamaka 10.3.
The Section on Full Understanding (Pariññāvāra) 10.3.4.
The Section on the Present and the Past (Paccuppannātītavāra)
10.3.4.1. Positive Order (Anuloma).
He who fully understands the eye-faculty has abandoned the faculty of mental grief? Yes.
Or conversely, he who has abandoned the faculty of mental grief has fully understood the eye-faculty? Yes.

Two types of persons have abandoned the faculty of mental grief (*domanassindriya*), yet they do not fully understand the faculty of the eye (*cakkhundriya*). One who possesses the supreme path (*aggamagga*) has both abandoned the faculty of mental grief and fully understood the faculty of the eye.
Does one who fully understands the faculty of the eye have cultivated the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" (*anaññātaññassāmītindriya*)? Yes.
Or rather, does one who has cultivated the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" fully understand the faculty of the eye?

Six types of persons have cultivated the faculty of “I shall come to know the unknown,” yet they do not fully understand the eye-faculty. One who possesses the path of supreme fruition has both cultivated the faculty of “I shall come to know the unknown” and fully understands the eye-faculty.
Is it the case that whoever fully understands the eye-faculty has cultivated the faculty of final knowledge (*aññindriya*)? No.
Or rather, is it the case that whoever has cultivated the faculty of final knowledge fully understands the eye-faculty? No.
Is he who fully understands the eye-faculty one who has realized the faculty of one who has already known? No.
Or again, is he who has realized the faculty of one who has already known one who fully understands the eye-faculty? No. (Based on the eye-faculty.
Is he who abandons the faculty of mental grief one who has cultivated the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown"? Yes.
Or again, does one who has cultivated the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" (anaññātaññassāmītindriya) abandon the faculty of mental grief (domanassindriya)?

Six types of persons have cultivated the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown," yet they do not abandon the faculty of mental grief. One who possesses the path of the non-returner (anāgāmimagga-samaṅgī) has both cultivated the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" and abandons the faculty of mental grief.
Does one who abandons the faculty of mental grief have cultivated the faculty of final knowledge (aññindriya)? No.
Or, whoever has cultivated the faculty of final knowledge (*aññindriya*), does that person abandon the faculty of mental distress (*domanassindriya*)? No.
Whoever abandons the faculty of mental distress, has that person realized the faculty of one who has already known (*aññātāvindriya*)? No.
Or, whoever has realized the faculty of one who has already known, does that person abandon the faculty of mental distress? No. (Based on the faculty of mental distress.)
Is it the case that whoever develops the faculty of “I shall come to know the unknown” has developed the faculty of final knowledge? No.
Or else, is it the case that whoever has developed the faculty of final knowledge develops the faculty of “I shall come to know the unknown”? No.
Is it the case that whoever develops the faculty of “I shall come to know the unknown” has realized the faculty of one who has already known? No.

Or, whoever has realized the faculty of one who has already known, does that person develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown"? No. (Based on the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown.
Whoever develops the faculty of final knowledge, has that person realized the faculty of one who has already known? No.
Or, whoever has realized the faculty of one who has already known, does that person develop the faculty of final knowledge? No. (Based on the faculty of final knowledge.)
10.3.4.2. Negative (Paccanīka) He who does not fully understand the faculty of the eye did not abandon the faculty of mental grief?

Two types of persons do not fully understand the faculty of the eye, yet they did not fail to abandon the faculty of mental grief. Six types of persons neither fully understand the faculty of the eye nor did they abandon the faculty of mental grief.
Or again, is it the case that whoever had not abandoned the faculty of mental grief (domanassindriya) has not fully understood the faculty of the eye (cakkhundriya)? Yes.
Is it the case that whoever has not fully understood the faculty of the eye has not cultivated the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" (anaññātaññassāmītindriya)?

Six types of persons have not fully understood the faculty of the eye, yet they have cultivated the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown. Two types of persons have neither fully understood the faculty of the eye nor cultivated the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown."
Or again, is it the case that whoever did not develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" (anaññātaññassāmītindriya) does not fully understand the eye-faculty (cakkhundriya)? Yes.
Is it the case that whoever does not fully understand the eye-faculty has not developed the faculty of final knowledge (aññindriya)?

An Arhat does not fully understand the eye-faculty, yet he has developed the faculty of final knowledge. Seven types of persons neither fully understand the eye-faculty nor have they developed the faculty of final knowledge.
Or, whoever did not develop the faculty of final knowledge (*aññindriya*) does not fully understand the eye-faculty (*cakkhundriya*)?

One who possesses the path of supreme fruition (*aggamagga*) did not develop the faculty of final knowledge, but he does not fail to fully understand the eye-faculty. Seven types of persons neither developed the faculty of final knowledge nor do they fully understand the eye-faculty.
Whoever does not fully understand the eye-faculty has not realized the faculty of one who has already known (*aññātāvindriya*)?

An Arahant does not fully understand the eye-faculty, yet he has not failed to realize the faculty of one who has already known. Eight types of persons neither fully understand the eye-faculty nor have they realized the faculty of one who has already known.
Or, conversely: whoever has not realized the faculty of one who has already known, does he not fully understand the eye-faculty?
One who possesses the path of the supreme fruit (Arahatta-magga) has not realized the faculty of one who has already known, yet he does not fail to fully understand the eye-faculty.
Eight persons neither had realized the faculty of one who has known, nor do they fully understand the eye-faculty.
(Based on the eye-faculty.
He who does not abandon the faculty of mental grief has not cultivated the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown"?

Six persons do not abandon the faculty of mental grief (*domanassindriya*), yet they have not failed to develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" (*anaññātaññassāmītindriya*). Two persons neither abandon the faculty of mental grief nor have they developed the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown.
Is it the case that whoever has not developed the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" does not abandon the faculty of mental grief? Yes.
Is it the case that whoever does not abandon the faculty of mental grief has not developed the faculty of final knowledge (*aññindriya*)?

An Arahant does not abandon the faculty of mental distress (*domanassindriya*), yet he has not failed to develop the faculty of final knowledge (*aññindriya*). Seven types of persons neither abandon the faculty of mental distress nor have they developed the faculty of final knowledge.
Or, conversely, is it the case that whoever has not developed the faculty of final knowledge does not abandon the faculty of mental distress?

One who possesses the path of the Non-returner (*anāgāmimagga*) has not developed the faculty of final knowledge, yet he does not fail to abandon the faculty of mental distress. Seven types of persons neither have developed the faculty of final knowledge nor do they abandon the faculty of mental distress.
Is it the case that whoever has not abandoned the faculty of mental distress (domanassindriya) has not realized the faculty of one who has known (aññātāvindriya)?

An Arahant has not abandoned the faculty of mental distress, yet he has realized the faculty of one who has known. Eight types of persons have neither abandoned the faculty of mental distress nor realized the faculty of one who has known.
Conversely, is it the case that whoever has not realized the faculty of one who has known has not abandoned the faculty of mental distress?
One who possesses the path of non-returning has not realized the faculty of one who has final knowledge, yet does not abandon the faculty of mental grief.
Eight types of persons have neither realized the faculty of one who has final knowledge nor do they abandon the faculty of mental grief.
(Based on the faculty of mental grief.)
Is it the case that whoever does not develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" has not developed the faculty of final knowledge?

An arahant does not develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown," yet he has developed the faculty of final knowledge. Seven types of persons neither develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" nor have they developed the faculty of final knowledge.
Or conversely, is it the case that whoever has not developed the faculty of final knowledge does not develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown"?

The person at the eighth stage (aṭṭhamaka) has not cultivated the faculty of final knowledge (aññindriya), but it is not the case that he does not cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" (anaññātaññassāmītindriya). Seven types of persons have neither cultivated the faculty of final knowledge nor do they cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown.
Is it the case that whoever does not cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" has not realized the faculty of one who has known (aññātāvindriya)?

An Arahant does not develop the faculty of “I shall come to know the unknown,” but he has not failed to realize the faculty of one who has already known. Eight types of persons neither develop the faculty of “I shall come to know the unknown” nor have they realized the faculty of one who has already known.
Is it the case that whoever has not realized the faculty of one who has already known does not develop the faculty of “I shall come to know the unknown”?

One who is at the eighth stage (the candidate for the fruit of stream-entry) has not realized the faculty of one who has already known, but he does not fail to develop the faculty of “I shall come to know the unknown.”
Eight persons neither have realized the faculty of one who has known (*aññātāvindriya*) nor are they developing the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" (*anaññātaññassāmītindriya*).
(Based on the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown.
Is it the case that whoever does not develop the faculty of final knowledge (*aññindriya*) has not realized the faculty of one who has known?

An Arahant does not develop the faculty of final knowledge (*aññindriya*), but he has not failed to realize the faculty of one who has already known (*aññātāvindriya*). Six types of persons neither develop the faculty of final knowledge nor have they realized the faculty of one who has already known.
Or rather: is it the case that whoever has not realized the faculty of one who has already known does not develop the faculty of final knowledge?
Three who possess the path have not realized the faculty of one who has already known, but they do not fail to develop the faculty of final knowledge.
Six persons have neither realized the faculty of one who has known nor are they developing the faculty of final knowledge. (Based on the faculty of final knowledge.)
